subject: [Fix][ROCm] MXFP4 MoE round-up inflates TP-sharded expert weights on CDNA3, starving KV cache (#56359)
pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #53961

While testing #53961, I found that the per-GPU VRAM used for weight loading is 135.35 GiB (without EP) vs 103.54 GiB (with EP). Upon closer investigation, it is caused by the rocm's branch of `mxfp4_round_up_hidden_size_and_intermediate_size` which rounds the intermediate moe size to 256 which inflated the expert weights usage. Before this PR, an existing special case for Kimi-K3 (AITER+SiLU/SiTU) already aligns to 128 instead of 256.

Concretely, for DeepSeek-V4-Pro (`moe_intermediate_size=3072`, TP=8, no EP):
- per-partition intermediate = 3072/8 = **384** fp4 elems (192 B)
- round_up(384, 256) = **512** → `w13_weight` created as `(384, 1024, 3584)` instead of `(384, 768, 3584)` → **+33% expert weights = +30 GiB/GPU**
- with the default `max_num_batched_tokens` (16384 since #51726), caused the observation from #53961 

EP wasn't affected because each GPU holds whole experts, so the intermediate dimension stays at its native 3072 (already aligned); without EP, TP slices it to 384 per GPU, which is not aligned and gets padded.

## Change

I extended the existing 128-alignment exception to also cover TRITON_UNFUSED with SiLU/SiTU activation. The pre-existing AITER arm is unchanged: K3's AITER kernel (gfx950-only) handles its native intermediate size (moe_intermediate 3072; e.g. 384/partition at TP8), so K3 keeps 128 on CDNA4.

For the new TRITON_UNFUSED arm, the 128-alignment is gated to CDNA != 4, because opt_flags_amd sets matmul_ogs's block_k=128 whenever weight scales are present on CDNA != 4 (always the case for mxfp4 W4A16 checkpoints) — the unpadded 384-element shard already satisfies the kernel's even-K requirement.  gpt-oss (SWIGLUOAI, tuned in #38043) keeps 256.

In essence, the checks keeps the pre-existing Kimi-K3, gpt-oss handling while letting DeepSeek-V4 Pro (TRITON_UNFUSED + SiLU/SiTU on CDNA3) keeps the 128 size without rounding up to 256. 

## Test Plan

Tested the before/after using this serve command:

```
# max batched tokens: 16384 will failed before this PR
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-siz …[truncated]
```

```
subject: [Bugfix] Mamba2 remove bugged initial state condition in chunk scan (#22034)
pr_body:
# Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist

## Purpose
This PR removes the condition that erroneously ignores `initial_states` tensor when batch size is 1.

```
            if initial_states.shape[0] == 1:
                # no in this case no point to use initial states
                initial_states = None
```

 Keeping it causes problem in batch size=1 prefill. For example, if the input batch contains only 1 long prefill request, when chunked prefilled is turned on, the prefill request will be processed in multiple `forward` iterations, which results in chunks 1, 2, ... to have valid initial_states. subject: [NPU] Fix DSA top-k seed buffer shape for MTP IndexShare (#31005)
```
pr_body:
## Motivation
PR #29787 introduced DSA top-k seed reuse from draft-extend to avoid recomputing the DSA indexer top-k in the draft-decode loop.

The seed buffers were allocated using the CUDA-style 2D layout:

```text
[num_tokens, index_topk]
```
However, the Ascend lightning indexer and sparse attention use a 3D TND sparse-index layout:
```text
[num_tokens, index_kv_heads, index_topk]
```
For the current NPU DSA implementation, the Index KV cache uses one MQA head, so the expected NPU seed shape is:
```text
[num_tokens, 1, index_topk]
```
The incorrect buffer shape caused two startup failures during graph capture:
With speculative_num_steps=1, copying the draft-extend indexer output into the 2D seed buffer failed with a broadcast shape error.
With speculative_num_steps>1, draft-decode graph capture passed a 2D sparse_indices tensor to npu_sparse_flash_attention, which requires a 3D tensor.
This PR enables NPU to use the draft-extend DSA seed reuse feature without disabling the optimization.

## Modifications

Updated the draft-extend graph capture buffer to use the platform-native seed shape.
Updated the draft-decode graph seed buffer to use the same platform-native shape.
Updated the eager draft-extend seed buffer allocation and reallocation logic to preserve all trailing dimensions.
Added validation for missing index_topk configuration.
Kept the existing NPU Draft Extend → Draft Decode DSA top-k reuse path enabled.
The NPU middle dimension is derived from the Index KV cache contract rather than index_n_heads. index_n_heads describes the lightning indexer's query heads, while sparse attention expects the sparse-index N dimension to match the single-head MQA Index KV cache.

subject: [Bugfix] ep_scatter kernel store-load race condition (#34991)
pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix an intra-CTA data race in `_fwd_kernel_ep_scatter_1` that causes sporadic "Warp Illegal Address" crashes during DeepGEMM MoE permutation (observed on DeepSeek V3 PD decode, but possibly affects any EP path using this kernel).

### The bug

The kernel launches 256 blocks × 256 threads (8 warps). Each block computes an exclusive prefix sum and writes **all** 256 entries of `expert_start_loc` to global memory via a vector `tl.store`, then loads back one entry via `tl.load(expert_start_loc + cur_expert)`.

The kernel distributes the vector store across threads, so thread `k` writes element `k`. With 8 warps, the store and load are not separated with a memory barrier. When block N loads `expert_start_loc[N]`, thread 0 (warp 0) may execute the load before thread N (warp N/32) commits its store. Since `expert_start_loc` is allocated with `torch.empty()` (uninitialized), the stale read returns garbage, which is used as an offset into `m_indices`. This causes a crash with an illegal address.

### The fix

Extract `cur_expert_start` from the prefix-sum register vector via `tl.sum(tl.where(...))` (a warp-shuffle reduction), then store that scalar to `expert_start_loc[cur_expert]`. This replaces the old pattern of writing a full 256-element vector to global memory and loading one element back. The scalar is used directly from registers (no race), and each block writes only its own entry to `expert_start_loc` (no redundancy). The next kernel sees the correct values via the implicit kernel-launch barrier.

### No need for pipelining

This PR also removes software pipeline staging in the later loop, because the loop only performs simple store and does not benefit from pipelining.

## Test Plan

This issue is not very easy to reproduce though, and I only observe it very occasionally. However, one can build a minimal reproduce example following the same pattern (vector `tl.store` + scalar `tl.load` on an uninitialized buffer) and see the data race after repeating several times.

Otherwise, I tested this PR the same as #20903:

subject: [NPU][bugfix] Fix NPU KernelLaunch Failure in rotate_input_ids_triton with Empty Batch (#30589)
pr_body:
## Motivation

This PR fixes an NPU runtime crash introduced by PR #28492 (Refactor / simplify MultiLayerEagleDraftExtendCudaGraphRunner to use rotation).
When extend_seq_lens has a batch size of 0 (e.g., a DP rank with no active requests), rotate_input_ids_triton launches a triton kernel with an empty grid. This violates NPU parameter verification rules and triggers the error:

> KernelLaunch failed because value 0 for parameter coreDim is invalid. Expected value: not equal to 0.

Root cause is confirmed via commit comparison: the issue does not exist on pre-PR commit bf231f01, and stably reproduces on merged commit 24bf8d91.

## Modifications

- Add an early return guard in rotate_input_ids_triton: when batch_size == 0, return input_ids directly without launching the kernel.
- This handles the empty batch edge case for DP ranks with no requests, and avoids invalid kernel launches on NPU platforms.

## Accuracy Tests

No accuracy impact. The fix only skips kernel execution for empty batches and does not alter behavior for valid inputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance impact. The added boundary check has negligible overhead and only takes effect on empty batch scenarios.

subject: [Fix] Support ENCODER_ONLY target-verify in the trtllm_mha backend (#32178)
pr_body:
Block-diffusion draft models (DFlash / DSpark) declare `AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY` on their layers: the draft block is trained with bidirectional intra-block attention, and backends like flashinfer honor it via `causal=False`. The trtllm_mha backend never reads `layer.attn_type` — its TARGET_VERIFY path always runs the trtllm-gen spec-decode kernel, which is causal inside the verify window, so the draft block silently loses bidirectionality (draft quality degrades; outputs stay correct since verify is lossless, which is why no accuracy test catches it).

This PR routes ENCODER_ONLY layers through the plain decode kernel over `bs * L` single-token rows whose kv length spans the whole window (block K/V are written to the pool before attention, so every row attends prefix + the full block). Metadata expansion is gated to draft workers running DFLASH/DSPARK — target workers and other draft algorithms are untouched — and is recorded in the same body as the existing fused graph-metadata refresh, so eager and CUDA-graph paths stay consistent.

`test_trtllm_mha_encoder_only.py` pins both semantics against a paged SDPA reference: the spec-decode call is causal-in-window, and the expanded formulation matches the full-window (bidirectional) reference.

subject: [Bugfix] Fix CUDA graph replay issues in trtllm_mla draft_extend (#21987)
pr_body:
## Motivation



Fix the test failure here https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/23877953915/job/69624981292
Same root cause and fix as PR #19807 

**Root cause**

`cu_seqlens_q` tensor layout differs in capture and replay path

In `init_forward_metadata_capture_cuda_graph`, `cu_seqlens_q` is built with a **uniform stride** via `torch.arange`.
In `init_forward_metadata_replay_cuda_graph`, the replay path was building `cu_seqlens_q` with a **variable stride** via `torch.cumsum(accept_length + 1)`. 


## Modifications



- Build `cu_seqlens_q` in the replay path using `torch.arange` with a fixed step of `num_draft_tokens`, matching the capture path.
- Set `max_seq_len_q` to the fixed `num_draft_tokens` instead of `max(accept_length) + 1`.
- Fill `seq_lens_q` with uniform `num_draft_tokens` instead of variable `accept_length + 1`.
- Use `self.num_draft_tokens` (from `server_args.speculative_num_draft_tokens`) instead of `self.speculative_num_steps + 1`, which doesn't exist on this backend.
- Remove the `accept_length_cpu` fast path — uniform stride makes the CPU-side path unnecessary.

## Accuracy Tests
Before fix this test will fail consistently. After fix this test passed 
`python -m pytest test/registered/spec/eagle/test_eagle_infer_beta_dp_attention_large.py::TestEagleDPAttnServerLarge -xvs`

subject: [Bugfix] Guard mixed-dtype allreduce RMSNorm quant fusions (#48330)
pr_body:
## Summary

Fixes #48324.

The residual FlashInfer allreduce + RMSNorm + static-quantization patterns could
match graphs where the activation and RMSNorm weight have different dtypes.

This occurs with Qwen/Gemma-style RMSNorm in
`nvidia/Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4`: the residual stream is BF16, while the effective
RMSNorm weight is FP32 due to the `weight.float() + 1.0` computation. Selecting
the fused quantized operation for this graph corrupts the hidden state and
produces repeated tokens such as `!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!`.

This change adds the existing `_norm_input_weight_dtype_match` compatibility
check to:

- `AllReduceFusedAddRMSNormStaticQuantFP8Pattern`
- `AllReduceFusedAddRMSNormStaticQuantNVFP4Pattern`

For incompatible mixed-dtype graphs, vLLM can still use the specialized fused
allreduce + Gemma RMSNorm path with `weight_bias=1.0`, followed by separate
quantization. Same-dtype models retain the complete allreduce + RMSNorm + quant
fusion.

## Why this was missed

The non-residual quantized patterns and ordinary residual RMSNorm patterns
already apply `_norm_input_weight_dtype_match`. The equivalent check was
missing from the two residual quantized pattern registrations introduced in
#21069.

## Regression test

The distributed fusion test now covers a Gemma-style RMSNorm model with:

- TP=2
- BF16 residual activations
- FP32 RMSNorm weights
- Static FP8 quantization
- FlashInfer TRT-LLM allreduce backend

The test verifies that the unsafe quantized fusion is rejected and the
dtype-aware Gemma RMSNorm fusion is selected with `weight_bias=1.0`.

## Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/compile/passes/distributed/test_fusion_all_reduce.py \
  -k "GemmaRMSNormStaticQuantFP8 and trtllm" \
  -v -s
```

Result:

```text
2 passed, 32 deselected
```

The MNNVL variants were not run because the test system has no NVSwitch and
does not support that topology. The TRT-LLM backend is the relevant backend for
this reproducer.

## Model validation

Tested with:

- `nvidia/Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4`
- 4× NVIDIA H100
- Tensor parallel size 4
- FlashInfer TRT-LLM allreduce backend
- Normal CUDA graph operatio …[truncated]

subject: [Helion] Fix degenerate scale_ub in kernel input generators (#48868)
pr_body:
## Purpose

The `generate_inputs()` for the per-block/per-token fp8 quant Helion kernels set
`scale_ub = torch.mean(input)`. The inputs are zero-mean (`torch.randn`), so
`mean(input) ≈ 0` (often slightly negative). Since `scale_ub` clamps the
per-group/per-token amax used to derive the quant scale, a ~0 upper bound
collapses every scale to `min_scaling_factor`, saturating essentially the entire
fp8 output.

The kernel and its autotune baseline then both produce the *same* saturated
output, so the autotuner accuracy check (and any correctness harness that
consumes these input generators) ends up comparing two saturated tensors and is
effectively a no-op for the `scale_ub` path.

## Fix

Set `scale_ub` to a non-degenerate upper bound, midway between the mean and the
max of the magnitude of the quantity that is actually clamped:

| op | clamped quantity |
|----|------------------|
| `silu_and_mul_per_block_quant` | SiLU-and-mul activation |
| `dynamic_per_token_scaled_fp8_quant` | `\|input\|` |
| `rms_norm_per_block_quant` | RMS-normed, weighted output |
| `rms_norm_dynamic_per_token_quant` | RMS-normed, weighted output |

`0.5 * (mean + amax)` keeps clamping *partially* active (some groups clamped,
some not) so both code paths are exercised. This mirrors the pattern already used
in `tests/kernels/helion/test_silu_and_mul_per_block_quant.py`.

## Test Plan

On `dynamic_per_token_scaled_fp8_quant` with the real `generate_inputs()` +
baseline:

- **Before:** `scale_ub ≈ -0.026` → **99.9%** of output saturated
- **After:** `scale_ub ≈ 2.05` → **~5%** saturated (normal for fp8 at the amax element)

All four op files produce healthy positive `scale_ub` values.

subject: [AMD] fix aiter cannot get heuristic kernel regression (#37438)
pr_body:
## Motivation


https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34647 introduced gluon into aiter backend also `SGLANG_AITER_MLA_GLUON` env is enabled by default. This behaviour change also introduces the regression for previous aiter asm path as below:
```bash
SGLANG_AITER_MLA_GLUON=0 \          <--------------- disable gluon to use aiter asm but server crashed
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 \
SGLANG_AITER_K3_OPT=1 \
AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE=1 \
AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /data-models/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code \
    --tp-size 8  \
	--prefill-attention-backend aiter \
	--decode-attention-backend aiter \
	--dtype bfloat16 \
	--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
    --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 32 \
	--max-mamba-cache-size 160 \
	--mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
    --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
	--tool-call-parser kimi_k3 \
    --host 127.0.0.1 \
	--port 8100 
```

Error message:
```bash
[AITER] /sgl-workspace/aiter/aiter_meta/csrc/py_itfs_cu/asm_mla.cu:193 get_heuristic_kernel_mla:
    cannot get heuristic kernel! q_type:bf16 kv_type:fp8 gqa:16 ps:0 prefill:0
    causal:1 qseqlen:1 lse:0 cprr:0
  Fatal Python error: Aborted
```

Root case is https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34647  wrongly disabled ps when gluon kernel is NOT being selected


## Modifications



Fix is trivial. We will disable ps only when gluon kernel is selected to avoid falling back to incorrect aiter kernel
